# Triage a red gate

<!-- gate-count:start -->

<!-- GENERATED by tools/src/gen/gen-gates.ts from docs/data/gates.json. Do not edit this paragraph. -->

**46 check gates** guard this repo: 46 run from `make` on your own machine and 46 on every
change in CI. Every one is listed in `docs/reference/gates.md`, generated from
`docs/data/gates.json`.

<!-- gate-count:end -->

Every finding names its gate in brackets — `[json-sanity] FAIL docs/data/gates.json:3: …` — and
that name is the gate's row id in [`gates.json`](../data/gates.json). Find the failing step
below, open its section, and run the command beside it to reproduce the finding alone.
`make validate` prints the same command, the repair and a link here under every red gate, so a
red run already tells you where to read.

## Type check

- **`TSnnnn <message>` on a file and line** — the compiler's own diagnostic, at the place it
  names. Fix the code there: tsx runs every gate without type-checking it, so this gate is the
  only place the error shows.
- **`TS5023 Unknown compiler option …` on `tools/tsconfig.json`** — the project file names an
  option this TypeScript version does not have. Remove it, or check the `typescript` pin in
  `tools/package.json`.
- **`FAIL: TSnnnn …` naming no file** — a diagnostic about the project as a whole, such as
  `TS18003 No inputs were found`: the tsconfig's `include` matches no file. Fix the list.
- **`tools/tsconfig.json: is missing`** — the project the check compiles is gone. Restore it
  from version control.
- **`tsc exited N and named no diagnostic`** — the compiler failed before it could report,
  usually because it is not installed. Run `make install`.

## JSON sanity

- **`<file>:<line>: is not valid JSON: …`** — the file does not parse at that line. Usually a
  trailing comma, a comment or an unquoted key; JSON allows none of them.
- **`<file>:1: opens with … — a data file opens with version, updated, note`** — a file under
  `docs/data/` does not start with its source header. Move `version`, `updated` and `note` to the
  top, in that order.
- **`version is not an integer`, `updated is not a year-month-day date`, `note is empty`** — the
  header is there but a value is the wrong kind. `updated` changes with every edit of the file.
- **`no JSON files found — the scan set is wrong`** — the gate read nothing, which is never true
  of this repo. It ran outside the checkout, or git listed nothing.
- **`no such file: <path>`** (exit 2) — a file named on the command line does not exist.

## Built output untracked

- **`<path>: is tracked, but … — git rm --cached it`** — a built file is in the index: an `.html`,
  something under `site/dist/`, `site/.astro/` or `site/coverage/`, `site/public/kb.js`, or a
  file under `site/src/content/docs/` other than the hand-written `index.mdx` and `404.mdx`. The site is built
  from `docs/`, so a tracked copy goes stale and doubles the diff. Run `git rm --cached <path>`;
  the build makes it again.
- **`.gitignore: lacks the line <line>`** — one of the seven build paths is no longer ignored.
  Put the line back verbatim; without it a build shows up as untracked files to add.

## Gate registry in sync

- **`<workflow>: no step named "X" — registered by <id>`** — the registry names a step the change
  workflow does not have. Add the step, or rename the row's `ci_step` to the step's real name.
- **`<workflow>: step "X" (job J) is in no registry entry`** — a named step checks something no
  row declares. Register it as a gate, or list it in `setup_steps` with why it checks nothing.
- **`<workflow>: step "X" is in job "J", registry says "K"`** — the step moved jobs. Update the
  row's `ci_job`, or move the step back.
- **`<workflow>: step "X" does not run the registry's command`** — the step's `run:` no longer
  contains the row's `wired` text. Make the two say the same command.
- **`<workflow>: step "X" has no if:`** — in a job holding several gates, a step without a
  condition is skipped once an earlier gate fails, hiding its findings. Add the `if:` the other
  gate steps carry.
- **`<workflow>: job "J" holds no gate and is in no reporting_jobs entry`**, or a
  `reporting_jobs` / `conditional_jobs` entry naming a job the workflow lacks — the job list and
  the registry disagree. Declare the job with its reason, or remove the stale entry.
- **`Makefile: has no <target> target`**, **`<target> does not run the collecting driver`** — a
  row's `local_target` names a target that is missing, or one that does not call
  `tools/src/run-gates.ts`.
- **`Makefile: <target> runs a gate no registry entry claims`** — a gate is wired into a
  gate-running target by hand. Register it instead; the driver runs every row.
- **`<program>: is a check gate no registry entry runs`** — a gate or generator program sits in
  `tools/src/gates/` or `tools/src/gen/` with no row. Register it with its CI step and triage
  section, or delete it.
- **`<id> runs <program>, which does not exist`** — a row's command names a program that is gone.
  Restore the program, or retire the row.
- **`docs/reference/triage.md: has no heading "#x" — <id> links there`** — a row's `runbook`
  anchor has no section on this page. Write the section, or fix the anchor.
- **`docs/reference/triage.md: its gate count block is stale`** — the count on this page no
  longer matches the rows. Run `make gates`.
- **`duplicate gate id`, `runs nowhere`, `runs_values does not define`, `has no wired command
  and no wired_note`, `positional is not true or false`** — a row itself is malformed. Fix the
  row in `docs/data/gates.json`.

## Gate reference in sync

- **`<output> is STALE — run: make gates`**, then diff lines — the output differs from what the
  registry renders: `<` lines are what the registry says, `>` lines what the file holds. Run
  `make gates` and commit the result with the registry edit; never edit generated lines by hand.
- **`<file>: lacks the <!-- name:start --> marker`** — a page that carries a generated block lost
  one of its markers. Put it back where the block belongs; the generator writes nothing to that
  page until it is there.
- **`<file>: is missing`** — a page the registry renders into is gone. Restore it; the generator
  never creates a hand-written page.
- **`docs/data/gates.json: is missing` or `is not valid JSON`** — the registry itself. Fix it;
  JSON sanity names the line.
- **`skipped docs/reference/gates.md: it does not carry this generator's stamp`** (a note, exit
  0) — a hand-written file sits where the generated reference belongs. Move it away, then run
  `make gates`.

## Test colocation

- **`<module>: has no test — add …`** — a module under `tools/src/` has no sibling test, no suite
  in its folder imports it, and no allowlist entry excuses it. Write the test; an entry is for a
  module that needs none, with the reason why.
- **`<hook>: has no test`** — a hook under `.claude/hooks/` has no test at
  `tools/src/hooks/<name>.test.ts` or `tests/hooks/<name>.test.sh`. Write one that runs it.
- **`<test>: is the test for <hook> by its path, but never names <hook>`** — the test sits where
  the hook's test belongs but does not run the hook. Make it run the hook by name.
- **`entry "x" excuses nothing`** — an allowlist entry whose thing now has a test, or is gone.
  Delete the entry.
- **`entry "x" has an empty reason`, `has no name`, `has no match`, `excuses a failure but names
  no owner`, `has no since date`** — an entry is malformed. Every entry says why; one excusing a
  failure also says who answers for it and since when.
- **`docs/data/allow/test-colocation.json: is missing`, `is not valid JSON` or `has no entries
  array`** — the allowlist itself. It exists even when empty.

## Context layers

- **`<dir>/CLAUDE.md: governed directory <dir>/ has no context layer`** — a top-level directory
  appeared without its layer. Write one in the same change: what the directory is, its
  conventions, a `Don't` heading and a link to the file that owns each detail. A directory that
  honestly needs none goes in `EXEMPT` in `tools/src/gates/check-claude-md.ts`, with its reason.
- **`<layer>: N words, budget B`** — the root or a directory layer holds a fact that belongs
  elsewhere. Move it to its single source and leave a link; compressing the prose to fit is not
  the fix. `docs/concepts/context-layering.md` says where facts go.
- **`<layer>: dead link: (<written>) resolves to <path>, which does not exist`** — the file the
  link routes to moved or went. Point the link at its new home, or delete the sentence with it.
- **`<layer>: no "Don't" heading`**, **`no repo-relative link`** — the layer is missing a
  required part. `make fix` opens the heading with a question under it; the finding stays until
  a person answers it. A heading or link inside a code fence does not count.
- **`<layer>: the "Don't" heading is empty`**, **`"<heading>" is empty`** — the heading holds
  only blank lines and comments, such as the question `make fix` wrote. Write the answer under
  it: one bullet per mistake actually made in the directory.
- **`<layer>: line copied from the root layer`** — the same long line (`DUP_MIN_LEN` characters
  or more) is in both files. Keep the copy in the file that owns the fact and link to it from the other.
- **`<path>/CLAUDE.md: a layer belongs at the root, at the top of a governed directory …`** —
  a layer sits off the governed set. Move its content into the directory's own layer, or, for a
  generated file that must stay until its builder retires, add an entry with owner, since and
  reason to `docs/data/allow/context-layers.json`.
- **`docs/data/allow/context-layers.json: entry "x" excuses nothing`** — the files it excused are
  gone. Delete the entry.
- **`FAIL: no governed directory found`** — every top-level directory is dot-prefixed or exempt,
  so the gate ran outside the checkout or `EXEMPT` swallowed everything.
- **`no layer governs: <path>`** (exit 2) — a narrowed run was handed a path under no layer, such
  as a root file or an exempt directory. Run the gate with no arguments.

## Command claims

- **`<file>:<line>: \`make <x>\` — the Makefile has no target <x>`** — a fence names a target that
  was renamed or removed. Rewrite the command to the target that does the job now; the claims
  rule, `.claude/rules/claims.md`, asks for that fix in the change that renamed it.
- **`` `make gate G=<stem>` — no gate or generator <stem>.ts ``** — the single-gate run names a
  program that is gone from `tools/src/gates` and `tools/src/gen`. Name the program that holds
  the check now, as its registry row's `command` does.
- **`\`<runner> <path>\` — <path> is not on disk`** — the script moved or retired. Point the
  command at its new path, or rewrite the sentence around what replaced it.
- **A command that is right but cannot be judged here** — one that runs in another checkout or
  after a step the fence does not show. End its line with `# claim-ok`, and say why in the same
  comment.
- **`<file>:<line>: <!-- x:start --> has no <!-- x:end --> on a line of its own`** — a marked
  block opens there and never closes, so the gate reads nothing after it. Put the end marker
  on a line of its own; if the start was only an example, move it into a code span.
- **`the tree has no Makefile`** — the gate ran outside the checkout.

## Trap inbox cap

- **`docs/inbox.md: N entries, cap 20`** — the inbox is full. Retire an entry by the ladder
  under "When an entry leaves" on that page: land its new home and delete the entry in the same
  change. Never raise the cap.
- **`docs/inbox.md:<line>: entry is N lines, limit 8`** — one entry has grown into a fact that
  wants a home. Move the detail to its tier on the ladder, and keep the entry short or delete it.
- **`docs/inbox.md:<line>: a top-level bullet that does not open with a bold phrase`** — a plain
  bullet at the top level (indented up to three spaces still counts), which the cap cannot
  count. Open it with the trap in bold, or indent it under the text of the entry it belongs to.
- **`docs/inbox.md:<line>: a numbered item outside "When an entry leaves"`** — a trap written
  as a numbered item, which the cap cannot count. Make it a bullet that opens with the trap in
  bold; only the exit ladder is numbered.
- **`docs/inbox.md: has no "## When an entry leaves" line`** — the page lost its contract, the
  exit ladder. Restore the heading exactly as written and the six tiers under it.
- **`docs/inbox.md: is missing`** — the page is gone. Restore it from version control; it exists
  even with no open traps.

## Harness shape

- **`.claude/<folder>: a folder under .claude/ with no row in the folder list`** — a new folder
  appeared under `.claude/`, often one a tool parked there. Add a row to `CLAUDE_DIRS` in
  `tools/src/gates/check-harness.ts` saying what its files are and what holds them, or move it
  out. Both harness gates read that one list.
- **`<entry>: an entry of .claude/skills/ is a folder holding SKILL.md, not a file`**,
  **`<entry>: a folder of .claude/skills/ with no SKILL.md`**, **`<skill>/SKILL.md: is a folder,
  not a file`** — a skill is a folder holding one `SKILL.md` file. Move a loose file into its
  own folder as `SKILL.md`, give an empty folder its skill file, or delete it.
- **`<entry>: an entry of .claude/<folder>/ is one .md file, not a folder`**, **`only .md files
  belong in …`** — an agent, a rule, a hook or a workflow is one file of its row's extension.
- **`<skill>/SKILL.md: has no name in its frontmatter`**, **`declares name: <x> but lives in
  <y>/`**, **`has no description in its frontmatter`** — a skill registers under its `name`,
  which is its folder's, and loads when a task matches its `description`. No allowlist entry
  excuses these.
- **`<skill>/SKILL.md:3: its description says …`** — the description lacks its trigger
  (`Use when …`), its boundary (`Not for …`) or both. A skill with no trigger never loads; one
  with no boundary loads for work it does not own.
- **`<file>:3: its description is <n> characters, over the cap of 350`** — the harness lists
  skill descriptions from one shared budget and drops what does not fit. Cut the description to
  what the skill does, a "Use when …" trigger with its three to five strongest phrases and a
  "Not for …" boundary naming the neighbour.
- **`.claude/skills: the skill descriptions hold <n> characters together, over the budget of
  16500`** — the sum across every skill; past it the harness stops offering the skills it cannot
  list. Shorten the longest descriptions first, or retire a skill.
- **`<file>:3: its description is not a quoted string and contains ": "`** — a plain YAML value
  with a colon and a space reads as a nested mapping under a strict parser. Wrap the whole
  value in double quotes (a skill's or an agent's).
- **`<file>:<line>: cites <page>.html#<id>`** — pages are markdown, so a harness file cites an
  element as `<page>.md#<id>`. Only a path starting `site/` or a `file://` URL may name a built
  `.html` page.
- **`<file>:3: its description is a YAML block scalar (>-)`** — the description is folded over
  several lines. The repo's one frontmatter reader, `scripts/fm-json.sh`, takes single-line
  values, so write it on one line.
- **`<skill>/SKILL.md: has no numbered steps`**, **`opens with a step`**, **`does not end with a
  "Done means" list`**, **`"Done means" is not its last section`**, **`"Done means" holds no
  list`** — the body is not gap, then numbered steps, then the done conditions. Copy the form
  of `.claude/skills/gate-red/SKILL.md`.
- **`<agent>.md: has no name in its frontmatter`**, **`declares name: <x> but the file is
  <y>.md`**, **`has no description in its frontmatter`** — an agent is launched by its `name`,
  which is its file's, and its description says when to launch it and when not.
- **`<agent>.md: declares no tools list`** — name every tool the agent may use in `tools`, and
  no more.
- **`<agent>.md: states no reply shape`** — the agent has no section headed as its reply. Add
  one (`## Reply`) holding the fixed shape its caller re-checks.
- **`<agent>.md:<line>: the claim verifier declares …`** (or the triage agent) — a verifier
  holds a tool beyond `Read`, `Glob` and `Grep`, or lacks one. A verifier with a shell or a
  writer can change the tree it reports on; put the list back to exactly those three.
- **`<agent>.md: its reply section lacks the shape …`** — a verifier's reply section lost part
  of the shape the spec fixes: the claim verifier's finding line (the page line, the claim, the
  tree line it cites, the severity) and its sentence saying it closes on exactly two lines, or
  the triage agent's five answers.
- **`<agent>.md: its reply section does not close on "checked: <n> claims on <page>" then
  "untestable:"`**, **`… puts a line after …`** — the claim verifier's reply ends on those two
  lines, one after the other, with nothing after them.
- **`.claude/agents/<name>.md: is missing`** — one of the two verifiers is gone. Restore it.
- **`<rule>.md: …`** — the rule's frontmatter: a description, and `paths` as an inline list of
  globs (a core rule always; another names the act it governs in an `act` key).
- **`.claude/hooks/<hook>: is not executable`**, **`exits N on …`**, **`prints on …`**, **`does
  not finish on … within N s`**, **`cannot be run on …`** — a hook must run by its path, and on
  an empty or non-JSON payload exit 0, print nothing and finish within its wired `timeout`
  (never more than 10 s). Run it by hand with `printf '' | .claude/hooks/<hook>` to see what it
  does.
- **`.claude/settings.json: is missing`**, **`is not valid JSON`** — the hooks are wired there.
  Restore the file, or make it parse.
- **`.claude/settings.json: wires <file>, which is not a hook`**, **`<hook>: is wired to no
  event`** — the wiring and the hooks folder disagree. Fix the command path in `settings.json`,
  or wire the hook, or delete it.
- **`docs/data/allow/harness-shape.json: entry "<skill>" excuses nothing`** — the list ships
  empty, and this entry's skill is in shape or gone. Delete the entry.
- **`docs/data/allow/harness-shape.json: is missing`**, **`entry "<skill>" has an empty reason`**
  — the allowlist itself. It exists even when empty, and an entry says why its skill keeps its
  old shape.

## Harness routes

- **`<file>:<line>: dead link: (<written>) resolves to <path>, which does not exist`** — the
  file the link routes to moved or went. Links resolve against the linking file's own folder, so
  a skill reaches the repo root with `../../../`. Point the link at the new home, or drop the
  sentence with it.
- **`<file>:<line>: points at <prefix>, which is untracked by design and nothing makes`** — a
  harness file sends a session to scratch space, such as `tmp/`, that exists only on its
  author's machine. Route the session to a tracked file, or to a tool's own folder that has a
  row with its command in `UNTRACKED` in `tools/src/gates/check-harness-routes.ts`.
- **`<file>:<line>: points at <prefix> without naming <command>`** — the path is build or tool
  output; name the command that makes it in the same file, so a fresh checkout can follow the
  route. A prefix counts only as a path token (a leading `./` is read past, so `./tmp/x` is
  `tmp/x`), and a mention belongs to the longest prefix it starts with.
- **`<file>:<line>: names <command>, which no permissions.allow entry in .claude/settings.json
  covers and PROMPT_KEPT does not list`** — a session following the file stops on a permission
  prompt. A read-only or repo-script command goes in `permissions.allow`, with the owner's
  agreement; one that writes or runs what it is handed goes in `PROMPT_KEPT` in
  `tools/src/gates/check-harness-routes.ts` with its reason, and in the table in
  [working-in-this-repo.md](../concepts/working-in-this-repo.md#commands-that-keep-their-prompt).
  The file is a skill, agent, rule or workflow, or a `CLAUDE.md` layer. A command is any line
  of a `bash`, `sh`, `shell`, `zsh` or `console` fence, and a line of an unlabelled fence or a
  code span whose first word is a known program; other fences (`text`, `json`) are not read,
  nor is a heredoc body. A placeholder (`<name>`, `…`) ends the command, which then shows as
  `<command> …`: only a `x:*` allow entry covers it, never an exact one. A placeholder inside a
  word (`scripts/<name>.mjs`) shows as `<start>…`, covered when an allow entry starts with it.
- **`.claude/settings.json: permissions.allow holds Bash(<entry>), which lets <write> run with
  no prompt`** — the allow list holds read-only and repo-script commands only. Drop the entry,
  or narrow it to a read (`git:*` to `git status:*`). `WRITES` in
  `tools/src/gates/check-harness-routes.ts` lists what counts as a write; `git add` is the one
  write the list keeps.

## Page frontmatter

Fix the page where it is, through `node scripts/kb.mjs set` where it has a flag.

- **`<file>: missing required key: <key>`** — the page block lacks the key, or declares it
  empty (`tags: []` included). `make fix` adds `title` from the H1 and `owner` from git, and a
  placeholder for any other key, filling an empty one where it stands.
- **`<file>: <key> is CHANGE-ME — only you can answer it`** — the placeholder `make fix` wrote.
  Replace it with the real value. For `status` the placeholder is all the repair writes: there
  is no default, because a default is how a draft comes to look finished, so choose `draft`,
  `stable` or `deprecated`.
- **`status "x"` or `area "x"` is not in its list** — the value is outside its closed list.
  `status` is listed in `tools/src/lib/page-block.ts`; an `area` is an area id of
  `docs/data/site-structure.json`. When the value looks listed, the finding says why it is not: this repo's one
  frontmatter reader keeps a trailing space and a trailing `# comment` as part of the value,
  where the site's YAML reader drops them. Delete the spaces, or move the comment to its own
  line.
- **`<file>:<line>: declares <key> N times`** — keep one line. This repo's reader takes the
  first, a YAML reader the last or none, so the two would disagree about the page. Until one
  line is left the key's value is not judged, and `make fix` leaves the lines as they are.
- **`tags is not an inline list`** — `tags:` is followed by indented `- a` lines. The parser
  reads a block list as empty, so every tag on the page is dropped: write `tags: [a, b]`.
- **`title "A" and H1 "B" disagree`** — the site shows one name and GitHub the other. Make them
  the same; a fenced `# comment` above the H1 is never read as it.
- **`key "x" is not in the page block`** — the block is closed. Delete the key, or add it to
  `PAGE_KEYS` in `tools/src/lib/page-block.ts` with the rule that holds its value.
- **`description contains ": " unquoted`** — invalid YAML for any real YAML reader. Rephrase
  with a dash, or quote the value.
- **`description is N characters`** or **`description is a block scalar`** — on every page and
  exercise, published or not, `description:` is one plain line of 160 characters or fewer. A
  published page also gets `PAGE-005` from the docs-style gate for the same line.
- **`dated records are not kept`** — a file sits under `docs/records/`. Delete it, and report
  the check's findings in the chat or in the issue its skill opens.
- **An exercise's findings** (`key "x" is not in the exercise block`, `type`, `area … must equal
  the folder`, `level is not an inline list`, `tags on an index`) — files under
  `docs/exercises/` carry only the exercise keys; the site computes the rest.
- **`not a markdown file under docs/: <path>`** (exit 2) — a named file is outside the page
  tree, or missing. Name a page, or run the gate with no arguments; naming
  `docs/data/site-structure.json` measures every page against it.

## Page shape

Every finding is `PAGE-00N <file>:<line> <message>` and ends with the rule's link on
[page-rules.md](page-rules.md), which says what the rule asks. A line of code, fenced or
indented four spaces outside a list, is never read. Named files only narrow the run: one the
structure file does not publish (the trap inbox, the map, an exercise, a stamped hub) is
skipped, as the whole run skips it.

- **`PAGE-000 docs/data/site-structure.json:1 is missing or is not JSON`** — the measured set
  is the pages it publishes. Restore it from git, or fix the JSON sanity finding.
- **`PAGE-001 … no intro paragraph before the first H2`** — open the page with a paragraph
  saying what it is and who it is for; a list, a table or a comment is no intro.
- **`PAGE-002 … heading deeper than H3`** — split the page, or turn the H4 into a paragraph that
  is one bold span.
- **`PAGE-003`** — the `## Next steps` section is not last, or holds no link or several. Keep
  one link in its list, the next page to read, and move any later section above it.
- **`PAGE-004 … N H1 headings`** — keep exactly one `# ` line outside the code fences.
- **`PAGE-005 … description is N characters`** — shorten `description:` to 160 characters or
  fewer, on one line: `node scripts/kb.mjs set <id> --essence "…"` on a KB page.
- **`PAGE-006 … raw URL in prose`** — wrap the address in a link, `[text](url)`.
- **`PAGE-008`** — the `## Next steps` section opens with its list, opens with two
  paragraphs or more, or has prose after it. Write one sentence, then the list, then nothing.
- **`no such file: <path>`** (exit 2) — a named file does not exist.

## KB page shape

Every finding is `KB-0nn <file>:<line> <message>` and ends with the rule's link on
[page-rules.md](page-rules.md). Fix the page where it is, through `node scripts/kb.mjs` where a
writer exists.

- **`KB-001 … no area of docs/data/site-structure.json lists this page`**, or **`area "x", but
  the row … is in area "y"`** — the page and its row disagree about where it sits: change the
  page's `area:` or move its row in `docs/data/site-structure.json` (the kb-move skill).
  **`KB-001 docs/data/site-structure.json:<line> the row … names <path>, which is not on
  disk`** — the page moved or went: point the row at its new path, or delete it.
- **`KB-002 … slug "x" is also <path>`** — two pages share a file name. Rename one; a slug
  names one page wherever the KB is read by id. The finding lands on the page no row lists, or
  on the later row.
- **`KB-003`** — a section with no `block` fact, a block the kind does not have, one twice, one
  out of order, or a required one missing. The kind's blocks, in order, are in
  `docs/data/content-model.json`.
- **`KB-004`, `KB-006`, `KB-007`, `KB-008`, `KB-009`** — the data layer: a suffix or fence
  meta (a `level=` token is retired: delete it), a section fact, a polarity or requirement
  group, or an id the dialect refuses (`tools/src/lib/dialect.md`, §3 and §7). The message is
  the dialect reader's own. A section fact sits on the line right under its heading, with no
  blank line between.
- **`KB-010 … sketch language "x"`** — name one of the sketch languages in
  `docs/data/content-model.json`, or `mermaid` for a figure. `go` is for a pattern page of the
  `concurrency` area only; anywhere else write the sketch in TypeScript.
- **`KB-013`** — `aliases` or `solves` is not an inline list, a page lists fewer than 3 or more
  than 5 `solves` (a theme lists none), a `solves` phrase runs past 20 words, or `favourite` is
  not `true`. `node scripts/kb.mjs set
  <id> --solves '[…]'` rewrites the list.
- **`KB-014 … the explain block …`** — the block is one paragraph of 60 to 180 words with no
  bold label, a costs list of 2 to 4 bullets (each a bold lead and at most 25 words; required on
  a pattern), then an `**Example.**` paragraph of at most 120 words or one captioned non-mermaid
  fence of at most 25 lines, and nothing else. `node scripts/kb.mjs explain <id> --text "…"
  --costs '[…]' --example "…"` writes it (with `--example-lang` and `--example-caption` for a
  sketch) and refuses a shape the rule rejects. A page that awaits its rewrite sits in an entry
  of `docs/data/allow/kb-shape.json` covering `explain` (a missing example or a word bound) or
  `costs` (a pattern's missing costs list), and nothing else is excused (one paragraph, no bold
  label, no level mark stay strict); delete the entry once its page passes, because the gate
  fails an entry that excuses nothing.
- **`KB-015 … the description …`** — the description block is one paragraph of at most 80 words.
  Cut it down to what the page is for; the rest belongs in the blocks below it. A page that
  awaits its rewrite sits in an entry of `docs/data/allow/kb-shape.json` covering `description`,
  whose `maxWords` is the length it had when listed: a page that grows past it fails. Delete
  the entry once the page passes.
- **`KB-016 … the selfcheck block …`** — the optional block holds exactly three blockquotes,
  each a bold question of at most 25 words ending in `?`, then an answer of at most 60 words
  that links at least one `page.md#element-id`. Fix the quote the finding numbers; the link gate
  tells you if a cited id does not exist. No allowlist excuses it.
- **`KB-000 docs/data/content-model.json:1` or `site-structure.json:1 is missing …`** — the
  gate has no closed lists or no rows to read. Restore the file from git.
- A named file the whole run does not measure (the trap inbox, the docs map, a layer) is
  skipped, never a finding.
- **`no such file: <path>`** (exit 2) — a named file does not exist.

## Docs map

Every finding is `[docs-map] FAIL <file>: <what>`. [The map](../README.md) links every page
under `docs/` directly, or through a hub it links (a `README.md` under `docs/`). Its table of
pages by area is built from `docs/data/site-structure.json` by `make map`; the rows above the
table are written by hand.

- **`<page>: no link from docs/README.md …`** — nothing on the map reaches the page. A page
  in the structure file gets its row from `make map` (its row there comes first, and
  `kb.mjs new` writes it for a new KB page); give any other page — a nested layer, a
  working file — a row by hand, in the change that adds it.
- **`docs/README.md: links <path>, which does not exist — fix the row or delete it`** — the page
  moved or went, or the row's case differs from the file's (the CI runner reads case exactly).
  Point the row at its new path; a row in the generated table follows the structure file, so
  run `make map`. A link in a code span or an HTML comment maps nothing: a commented-out row
  leaves its page unlinked.
- **`<hub>: links <path>, which does not exist`** — the same, one level down, in a hub the map
  links. Fix the hub's link.
- **`docs/README.md: is missing`** — the map is gone, and nothing else is checked until it is
  back. Restore it.
- **`unknown argument`** (exit 2) — the gate takes no arguments; the whole tree is always
  measured.

## Docs map in sync

- **`docs/README.md is STALE — run: make map`**, then diff lines — the table between
  `<!-- docs-map:start -->` and `<!-- docs-map:end -->` is not what the structure file renders:
  `<` lines are the render, `>` lines the file. Run `make map`; never edit the table by hand,
  since a page's label, area and order live in `docs/data/site-structure.json`.
- **`docs/README.md: lacks the <!-- docs-map:… --> marker`** or **`is missing`** — put the
  marker or the page back; the generator never writes a page that lost its markers.
- **`docs/data/site-structure.json: is missing`, `is not valid JSON` or `has no areas list`** —
  the structure file. Restore it from git; JSON sanity names a bad line.

## Diagrams parse

Every finding is `[mermaid-parse] FAIL <file>:<line>: diagram does not parse — <message>`. The
gate reads each ```` ```mermaid ```` fence under `docs/` and hands it to the mermaid the site
build draws with, which runs the grammar and draws nothing, so the whole tree takes seconds.

- **`Parse error on line N:`** or **`Lexical error on line N`** — the line the finding names is
  the file line mermaid blamed; the message's rest, which `make gate G=check-mermaid` prints,
  says what it expected there. A missing arrow end, an unquoted label holding brackets or a
  colon, and a `click` line with no target are the usual causes.
- **`No diagram type detected`** — the fence's first line is not a diagram keyword
  (`flowchart`, `sequenceDiagram`, `classDiagram`, `stateDiagram-v2`, `erDiagram`, …). A fence
  labelled `mermaid` that holds something else wants another label.
- **`no such file`** (exit 2) — a file named on the command line is not there. With no files
  the gate reads every markdown file git lists under `docs/`.

## Repository links

Every finding is `[repo-links] FAIL <file>:<line>: <what>`, on the line of the link. The gate
reads every markdown file git lists except built output and `node_modules/`. A link inside
code (fenced, or indented four spaces outside a list), an inline code span or an HTML comment
is not read. `make validate-changed` runs the gate whole, because moving one file can break a
link in another.

- **`links <path>, which does not exist`** — the target moved or went, or its case differs from
  the file's: macOS finds `Page.md` for `page.md`, the CI runner does not. Link its new path,
  in the change that moved it; a directory counts as present. A target like `docs:page.md` is a
  dead path, not an address: only `http`, `https`, `mailto`, `tel`, `data`, `javascript`, a
  scheme followed by `//`, and `//` itself are external.
- **`links <target>, which climbs out of the repository`** — too many `../`. Count the linking
  file's folders again.
- **`links <file>#<fragment>, and <file> has no heading or id "<fragment>"`** — the heading was
  reworded or the anchor removed. A heading's anchor, ATX or setext, is its text as a reader
  sees it (emphasis marks gone, an underscore inside a word kept) lower-cased, punctuation
  dropped and spaces turned to hyphens; a repeat gains `-1`, `-2`. An `id` or `name`
  attribute counts, and on a page under `docs/` so does every element id the markdown
  dialect gives (a block name, a `{#id}`, a positional id such as `tradeoffs-con-2`).
- **`the label names <path>, and the link goes to <file>`** — a label that is only a path
  names a different file than the target. Fix whichever is wrong; the label may be written
  from the linking file's folder, the repository root or `docs/`.
- **`not a markdown file git lists: <path>`** (exit 2) — a named file is not a tracked or
  untracked-but-not-ignored markdown file. Name one, or run the gate with no arguments.
- **`unknown argument`** (exit 2) — the gate takes file names and no flag, `--fix` included.

## Vocabulary bans

The ban gate. It reads `docs/data/glossary.json` first, then every markdown file git lists —
committed or not, minus ignored files, the fixture trees and changelogs — and fails each prose line that uses a phrasing a term bans. Code spans, fences
(inside a blockquote or a list item too), raw HTML `<code>` and `<pre>`, frontmatter keys, the
`solves` and `aliases` values (a searcher's words and a thing's other names, which search must
still match), link targets, HTML tags and comments, and a trailing `{#id}` suffix are not prose;
a tracked file deleted but not yet staged is left out. The words and their replacements are
listed on the [glossary](glossary.md).

- **`<file>:<line>: use "<term>" not "<phrasing>" — also fine: …`** — rewrite the line in the
  word the finding names, or one of its also-fine words, choosing it for the sense: a value
  worked out from others is computed, a class that extends another is a subclass. Fix it where
  the line comes from: in a page, the `explain`, `production` and `wild` blocks through
  `node scripts/kb.mjs explain`, `production` or `wild`, dumping the block with
  `get <id> --block <b> --json` first so no level tag or `<code>` is lost. A generated file
  names its generator in its stamp; fix the generator's source.
- **A line that has to name the phrasing** — a style rule quoting what it bans, say. Put
  `<!-- vocab-ok -->` on that line; it frees that line only, and never inside a code span.
- **A file that has to keep the phrasing** — a working plan written in the words of its day,
  say. Add a reasoned entry to `docs/data/allow/vocabulary.json` whose `match` is that file,
  with `owner` and `since`: a banned phrasing is a failure, so every entry owes both. The whole
  run fails the entry once the file is clean, and it is deleted then.
- **`docs/data/glossary.json: term <id>: missing <field>`**, **`see names <b>, which does not
  list <a> back`**, **`banned phrasing "<x>" belongs to more than one term`**, **`unknown
  scope`**, **`duplicate id`**, **`"<w>" is a word to write here and a banned phrasing of <id>`**
  — the glossary itself is unsound, and no prose is read until it is fixed. Fix
  `docs/data/glossary.json`, then `make glossary`.
- **`docs/data/allow/vocabulary.json: entry "<name>" excuses nothing`** — every file the entry
  matches is clean now. Delete the entry. `… has an empty reason`: say why the files may use a
  banned phrasing, or delete the entry. `… excuses a failure but names no owner` or `… has no
  since date`: give the entry the person who answers for it and the day it was added.
- **`FAIL: no markdown file to scan — the scan set is wrong`** — git listed no markdown file:
  the gate ran outside the checkout.
- **`no such file: <path>`** (exit 2) — a file named on the command line does not exist.

## Glossary reference in sync

`docs/reference/glossary.md` is rendered whole from `docs/data/glossary.json` by
`tools/src/gen/gen-vocabulary.ts`. Never edit it by hand.

- **`FAIL: docs/reference/glossary.md is STALE — run: make glossary`**, then diff lines — the
  page and the data disagree. Run `make glossary` (or `make gen`) and commit both.
- **`docs/data/glossary.json: …`** — the data has a fault the ban gate names too; the page is
  not rendered from it. See [Vocabulary bans](#vocabulary-bans).
- **`skipped docs/reference/glossary.md: it does not carry this generator's stamp`** (a note,
  exit 0) — a hand-written file sits at the output path. Move it away, then run `make glossary`.

## Search synonyms hold their rules

`docs/data/search-synonyms.json` bridges the words a searcher types to the words the pages use;
`kb.mjs find` reads it. A bridge that breaks a rule never fires or fires on the wrong pages, and
nothing else says so. Every finding names the layer and the key; fix it in the data file, then
run `make synonyms` so the reference page follows.

- **`a key is a lowercase word of two letters or more, letters only`** or **`a stopword`** —
  the scorer never sees that key. Pick the word a searcher types that meets the rule.
- **`<n> targets — a key names 1 to 4`**, **`names "<word>" twice`**, **`names itself`** — trim
  the list to the words that bridge.
- **`"<word>" is in no page's declared facts, so it matches nothing`** — the target is not a
  word of any page's slug, title, description, aliases, tags or `solves`. Pick one the pages use.
- **`"<word>" contains the key, which already matches it`** — an expansion's target the key
  finds by substring anyway. Drop it.
- **`out of order, after "<key>"`** — keep the expansion keys sorted.
- **`curated holds the key too … merge it into curated`** — curated takes its value whole, so
  the expansion is dead. Move the words you want into the curated entry and delete the other.
- **`expansionMeta.entries is <n>, and expansions holds <m> keys`** — set `entries` to the count.
- **`is missing`** or **`is not valid JSON`** — restore the file from git, or fix the syntax.

Whether a target means the same thing in this corpus, or is too broad to help, no gate can
tell: that judgement is the kb-vocab skill's.

## Search synonyms reference in sync

`docs/reference/search-synonyms.md` is rendered whole from `docs/data/search-synonyms.json` by
`tools/src/gen/gen-search-synonyms.ts`. Never edit it by hand.

- **`FAIL: docs/reference/search-synonyms.md is STALE — run: make synonyms`**, then diff lines —
  the page and the data disagree. Run `make synonyms` (or `make gen`) and commit both.
- **`docs/data/search-synonyms.json: …`** — the table breaks a rule the synonyms gate names too;
  the page is not rendered from it. See [Search synonyms hold their rules](#search-synonyms-hold-their-rules).
- **`left docs/reference/search-synonyms.md alone: it does not carry this generator's stamp`** —
  a hand-written file sits at the output path. Move it away, then run `make synonyms`.

## Search oracle answers

`docs/data/search-oracle.json` lists queries a person typed and what the first hits must be. The
gate runs each one through the search box's ranking (over the page tree) and through `kb.mjs
find`; a finding ends in `(site)` or `(cli)` for the path that missed, and both paths usually
miss together. A case marked `"via": "cli"` is held to `find` alone, because the search box reads
a page's declared facts only and is not expected to answer a long description: its findings end
in `(cli)`.

- **`<query> → got <id>, wanted <id> or <id> (site|cli)`** — the first hit is not one of the
  wished pages. Read the two rankings with `node scripts/kb.mjs find "<query>"`. If the query
  names nothing the pages say, add a synonym through the kb-vocab skill; if the wish is wrong,
  edit the case.
- **`<query> → got <ids>, wanted the first <n> of kind <kind>`** (or `band`) — a hit of another
  kind or band is among the first `n`. Scope the query by hand with `--kind` or `--band` to see
  what crowds the list.
- **`<query> → got <id> at <rank> (…), wanted it within the first <n>`** (or `absent`) — the page
  fell below its rank. The same reading as the first bullet.
- **`<query> → got <k> hits (…), wanted <n> of kind <kind>`** — fewer hits than the case asks
  to look at.
- **`<query> → got <k> of <count> in the first <n> (<hits>), wanted <min>; missing <ids> (site|cli)`**
  — a `covers` case: fewer of its pages are among the first `n` hits than the case asks for.
  The query describes a problem, and the pages that answer it rank lower or not at all. Fix it
  in this order. First, read the query as a person would type it: a symptom and a constraint,
  with no pattern, product or page name in it. A query that names a page finds it for the wrong
  reason, and one nobody would type fails for the right one, so rewrite it. Second, read the
  ranking with `node scripts/kb.mjs find "<query>" --n 20` and add the synonym the missing page
  needs to `docs/data/search-synonyms.json` through the kb-vocab skill. Last, change the ranking
  in `tools/src/lib/search-score.ts`: it moves every other query, so rerun this gate and
  `make tools-test T=relevance`. Never lower `min`, drop an id or widen `n` to land a change
  without the owner's say. The case records what the ranking reaches, and a lower number hides
  a loss.
- **`case <n> "<query>": `top` names "<id>", which is no page`** — an id in the case is no
  page of the tree. The page was renamed or retired: edit the case. The same finding names
  `within`, and `covers.ids` for a case's `covers`.
- **`case <n>: unknown key`**, **`expects nothing`**, **`n means something only beside kind or band`**,
  **`covers.min is <m>, more than its <k> ids`** (or more than the `n` hits it looks at),
  **`covers.ids names "<id>" twice`**, **`via is not one of cli`** — the case's shape; the
  note in `docs/data/search-oracle.json` lists the forms.
- **`docs/data/search-oracle.json: is missing`** — restore it from git.

## Product registry

The offline half of the vendor-link audit: `docs/data/products.json` against the mapping tables
of `docs/capabilities/*.md`. Every fix goes into `docs/data/products.json`.

- **`<provider> "<name>" is registered but no mapping cell in its column says it`** — no page
  renders the link. Delete the entry, or name the product in a mapping cell of that provider's
  column.
- **`<provider> "<name>" appears only in the <other> column`** — the entry would send a reader
  to the wrong provider's documentation. Move it under the provider whose column says it.
- **`… is not https`**, **`… points at a bare homepage rather than documentation`**,
  **`… has an unparseable URL`** — give the entry the product's documentation URL, fetched and
  answering 200. Fetch it yourself before adding it, then run `make products`.
- **`docs/data/products.json: is missing` / `is not valid JSON` / `` `columns` `` or
  `` `products` `` shape** — restore the file from git, or fix the shape the finding names.
- **`FAIL: no capability page under docs/capabilities/`** — the pages the registry is held to
  are gone, or the gate ran outside the checkout.
- **The worklist** — `make gate G=check-products ARGS=--worklist` lists the mapping-cell
  fragments no entry names. It is never a finding: whether a fragment is a product is a
  judgement.
- **The online half, `make products`** — fetches every URL (HEAD, then GET where HEAD is
  refused), a few at a time. It needs the network, so it is no gate and never runs in
  `make validate` or CI; run it by hand before a release or after editing the registry.
  **`… answers <status>`** means the vendor moved or removed the page: find where it went, or
  drop the entry. **`… did not answer (<reason>)`** may be the network rather than the vendor:
  fetch the URL yourself before changing anything.

## Relations closed and paired

`docs/data/relations.json` is the source: fix the record at the line the finding names
(`node scripts/kb.mjs link` and `unlink` write whole edges), then run `make gen`. A record's
finding opens with its edge, `<a> <verb> <b>`.

- **`is missing`** or **`is not valid JSON`** — against `relations.json`, `content-model.json`
  or `site-structure.json`: the gate reads the edges from the first, the closed verbs from the
  second and the published pages from the third, and checks nothing further until all three
  read. Restore a missing one from git.
- **`has no note_b — b's side of the edge is missing`** — the one-way edge of the HTML era: one
  page declares it and the other does not. Write the missing side's note (`""` for none), or
  drop the record.
- **`"x" is not one of the 19 verbs`** — the verbs are closed. Pick one from `relations.verbs` in
  `content-model.json`, or add a verb there first through the vocabulary skill.
- **`writes "has-variant", the second verb of its pair — write it as …`** — an edge has one
  spelling, from the page whose verb is listed first. The finding spells the record to write
  instead, with the two notes swapped.
- **`<a> is exposed to a hazard, so it must be a pattern or a design`**, **`<b> threatens <a>, so it must be a hazard`** —
  `exposed-to` runs from a pattern or a design to a hazard. Use `combines-with` for any other
  pair, or swap the pages if the hazard was written first.
- **`relates a page to itself`**, **`<slug> is no published page`** — a slug typo, or a page
  renamed or unpublished without its edges. Fix the slug, or drop the edge with the page.
- **`repeats the edge at line N`** — the pair carries this verb family twice, which includes a
  symmetric verb written once from each side. Keep one record and merge the notes.
- **`contradicts line N, which says …`** — the pair says both `x variant-of y` and
  `y variant-of x`. Decide which page is the narrower one and delete the other record.
- **`group_a is not a heading`**, **`group_a "…" is the verb's own label`** — a custom group
  heading exists only to differ from the verb's label. Drop the key, or write the heading.
- **`maps_a sits on <slug>'s side, which reads "…"`** — only the `implements` side of a
  capability or comparison page maps to a row of its table. Move the key to that side, or
  drop it.
- **`maps_a "mapping-row-N" names no row of <slug>'s mapping or matrix table`** — row ids are
  positional (`<block>-row-N`), so a row added above it renumbered the table. Point the key at
  the row's new id.
- **`group_order.<slug> pins "…" twice`**, **`… a group none of its edges sit under`**,
  **`group_order names <slug>, which is no published page`** — the pinned order lists a heading
  the page no longer has. Remove it from the list; a heading the list leaves out renders after
  the pinned ones.

## Learning paths resolve

`docs/data/learning-paths.json` is the source: fix the stage or note the finding names, then
run `make gen`. A page move changes its stage in the same change as its structure row. A finding names the profile by its `id`, which is the theme
page's slug.

- **`profile 'x' stage /route is not a route docs/data/site-structure.json produces`** — the page
  moved, was renamed or was unpublished, and the stage kept the old route. Write the route the
  structure file lists for it. Ending **`— it is spelled /route.html there`**, the page is there
  and only the spelling differs: stages are compared exactly, so copy the structure file's form.
- **`stages /route twice`** — a tour visits a page once. Drop the second stage.
- **`stages /route, whose page declares status draft`** — a draft sits on no reading order.
  Finish the page and mark it `stable`, or drop the stage until it is.
- **`names no published page`**, **`is listed twice`**, **`level … is not one of …`**, **`has no
  label`**, **`has no stages list`**, **`unknown key`** — the profile record is broken. A
  profile's `id` is the slug of the page its tour renders on.
- **`notes[/route].x is an orphan`** — a note for a route its profile does not stage, or for a
  profile that does not exist, renders nowhere. Delete it, or add the stage it was written for.
- **`has no tour`**, **`heading is empty`**, **`stepLevel "basic" is not advanced or expert`** — a
  note carries `role`, `tour` and `fluency` (`""` for none), a `heading` only when it differs
  from the member's title, and a level key only above `basic`.
- **`is not valid JSON`**, or the structure file **`is missing`** — the gate checks nothing
  further. A missing learning-path file is no finding: there is no stage to check.
- **`note: N published route(s) on no learning path`** on stderr — information, never a finding.
  Most hazard, principle, case-study and reference pages sit on no tour.

## Tracks resolve

`docs/data/tracks.json` is the source of the home page's Start-here block: fix the track or
tier the finding names there, then run `make gen`. A finding names the track by its `id`, and a
theme by its slug, which is also its profile id in `docs/data/learning-paths.json`.

- **`has N tracks — the home page shows 4 to 6`**, **`walks N themes — a track walks 3 to 6`** —
  the count is outside the range. Add or drop a track or a theme; a track is a short path, not a
  list of everything.
- **`theme 'x' is no profile id of docs/data/learning-paths.json`** — a step is a theme with a
  tour. Write the slug of a theme that has a profile, or add the tour first.
- **`theme 'x' is no published theme page`**, **`declares status draft`** — the theme moved, was
  renamed or is unfinished. Write the slug the structure file lists, or drop the theme until the
  page is `stable`.
- **`lists theme 'x' twice`**, **`is listed twice`**, **`has no id`**, **`has no label`**, **`has
  no blurb`**, **`has no themes list`**, **`unknown key`** — the track record is broken. A track
  holds `id`, `label`, `blurb` and `themes`, and nothing else.
- **`tier of 'x' is … — a tier is one of intro, core, advanced`**, **`tier names 'x', which is
  no published page`** — fix the tier word, or the slug it is keyed by.
- **`theme 'x' is staged by a track and has no tier`** — add the theme to `tiers`. A tier lives
  in this file, never in a page's frontmatter.
- **`is not a JSON object`**, or the structure file **`is missing`** — the gate checks nothing
  further. A missing tracks file is no finding: there is no track to check.

## Tour order holds

A theme's tour is the `stages` of its profile in `docs/data/learning-paths.json`, in reading
order; the `prerequisite` edges are in `docs/data/relations.json`, where `a requires b`. A page
must come after every page it requires that is also in the same tour. A finding names the
theme (the profile's `id`), the page that comes too early, the prerequisite and the 1-based
position of each, at the line of the early stage.

- **`theme 'x': a (stage 2) comes before its prerequisite b (stage 5)`** — move the stage of `b`
  above `a` in `docs/data/learning-paths.json`. The notes are keyed by route, so they follow the
  stage; then run `make gen`, which rewrites the tour block and the fluency blocks in that order.
  When the edge itself is wrong, unlink it in `docs/data/relations.json` (through
  `node scripts/kb.mjs unlink`) instead.
- **`is missing`**, **`has no relations list`**, **`has no profiles list`** — the file the gate
  reads is broken; the relations, structure and learning-paths gates name the cause. A missing
  learning-paths file is no finding: there is no tour to order.

## Prerequisite graph holds

`docs/data/prerequisites.json` says what to read before a page and what to read beside it. It
is built from `docs/data/relations.json` — a record's `requires` is its `prerequisite` edges,
its `related` its symmetric ones — so fix an edge there, never in the graph (through
`node scripts/kb.mjs link` or `unlink`), then run `make prerequisites`. A finding about an
edge — a cycle, a stable page requiring a draft, an orphan — sits at the line of that edge in
`docs/data/relations.json` whenever the relations file holds it; any other finding sits at
the line of the record it is about.

- **`lacks its source header`**, **`is not valid JSON`**, **`is missing`** — the file is judged
  no further. `make prerequisites` rewrites it.
- **`records 'a' and 'b' require one another round a cycle`**, **`requires itself`** — no page
  in the cycle can be read first. Unlink one of the `prerequisite` edges; the finding names
  every page on the cycle and the relations-file line of every edge on it.
- **`lists as related 'b' twice`**, **`requires 'b' twice`** — a page appears once in a list.
  The generator lists a pair joined by two symmetric verbs once, so from `make prerequisites`
  this means the graph was edited by hand.
- **`requires 'x', which no record declares`**, **`route /r is not a route … produces`** — an
  edge to a page that left the graph, or a page that moved. Both come from the relations file
  and the structure file; fix them there.
- **`lists 'b' as related, but 'b' does not list 'a'`**, **`lists itself as related`** — a
  related pair is listed both ways and joins two pages.
- **`is an orphan`** — nothing requires the page, nothing lists it as related, and no learning
  path stages it, so no reader path leads there. Give it an edge or a stage, or add an entry
  with its reason to `docs/data/allow/prerequisites.json`, matched against the route. Its one
  entry today covers the capability and comparison pages, which are always the page that
  requires; **`entry "x" excuses no record`** means that cause is gone, so delete the entry.
- **`is stable but requires 'x', whose page is a draft`** — a finished page cannot send its
  reader to an unfinished one. Finish the draft, or mark the requiring page `draft` too.

## Prerequisite graph in sync

`docs/data/prerequisites.json` and `docs/reference/prerequisites.md` are the relations file's
second form, built by `tools/src/gen/gen-prerequisites.ts` from the relations file, the pages'
titles and descriptions and the structure file. `make prerequisites` rewrites both, and
`make gen` runs it after the relationships and tour generators.

- **`is STALE — run: make prerequisites`** — an output was edited by hand, or an edge, a title
  or a description changed without the rebuild. Run it and commit both outputs with the change.
- **`names x, which is no published page`**, **`declares no title`**, **`declares no
  description`** — nothing is written until the source is whole. The relations gate says more
  about an edge; the page's frontmatter is the place for the other two.

## Relationships blocks in sync

- **`<page> is STALE — run: make gen`**, then diff lines — the page's relationships marked
  block is not what `docs/data/relations.json` renders: `<` lines are the render, `>` lines
  the page. Run `make gen`; never edit the block by hand, since every row is an edge record and
  its note. A page that quotes a block's start or end marker literally, even in a code span,
  counts as holding that block.
- **`<page>: lacks the relationships start or end marker`** or **`is missing`** — a page an edge
  names has lost its block, or the page is gone. Put the two markers back under the
  relationships heading, or remove the edge in the same change as the page.
- **`docs/data/relations.json: … — run: make gate G=check-relations`** — an edge the renderer
  cannot draw (an end, a note or a verb it does not know). The relations gate says which;
  nothing is written until it is fixed.

## Tour and fluency blocks in sync

- **`<page> is STALE — run: make gen`**, then diff lines — a theme's tour block or a member's
  fluency block is not what `docs/data/learning-paths.json` renders. Run `make gen`; a stage, a
  role or a note changes in the data file, once, for both pages.
- **`<page>: lacks the tour start or end marker`** (or the fluency one) or **`is missing`** — a page a
  profile stages has lost its block, or the page is gone. Put the markers back, or move the
  stage in the same change as the page.

## Structure file

`docs/data/site-structure.json` lists every published page, its area and its place in reading
order. It is edited by hand, so every finding is repaired there.

- **`docs/data/site-structure.json: area 'x' is not in the closed area list (AREAS in
  site/src/lib/types.ts)`**, or **`site/src/lib/types.ts: AREAS lists 'x', which no area …
  declares`**, or **`AREAS runs in another order`**, **`AREAS lists 'x' more than once`**,
  **`AREAS holds N areas and … M`** — the two lists hold one sequence, each area once. Add,
  remove or move the id in `AREAS` in the same change as the area; a site schema refuses every
  page of an area the list does not hold. An id commented out of `AREAS` is not in it.
- **``site/src/lib/types.ts: no `const AREAS = [...]` holding only quoted ids``** — the gate reads
  the tuple as text, and it is no longer one flat list of quoted ids with commas between them
  (comments are fine). Write it back in that shape rather than building it from another list.
- **`area #n is not an object`**, **`area '<a>' row #n is not an object`** — an entry is `null`,
  a string or a list. Write it as an object with its fields, or delete it; the other entries
  were still checked.
- **`area '<a>' page '<p>': route <r> is already taken`** — two rows, or a row and an area's
  `/<id>/`, claim one route. Give one of them its own `route`, or rename the slug.
- **`area '<a>' page '<p>': file name 'x' is also a page in area '<b>'`** — a reader's favourite
  and practiced marks are stored under the page's file name, so two published pages in different
  areas that share one would share a mark. Rename one page's file (the kb-move skill moves a
  page and its row together); an area with `nav: none` is unpublished and not counted.
- **`… source <path> does not exist`**, **`… is not a page under docs/`**, **`… no source`** — a
  row points at nothing. Point it at the page under `docs/`, or delete the row.
- **`… source 'generated' but area '<a>' declares no generator`** — only an area that names its
  generator in `generated` may hold a row that generator writes.
- **`… source 'site' but no committed page at …`**, or **`site/src/content/docs/<page>: not listed
  in docs/data/site-structure.json`** — a hand-written site page and its `site` row go together:
  add the row, or move the page out of the input folder. Only a page git tracks counts, so
  `git add` a new page with its row; a page is output, and exempt, only when a line of its own
  is a whole-file stamp — mentioning one in the text does not count.
- **`area id 'x' is not kebab-case`**, **`declared twice`**, **`has no label`**, **`hub has no
  description`**, **`nests under 'x', which is no other declared
  area`** — the area's own record is incomplete; fill it in the structure file.
- **`area '<a>' nav "x" is not one of link, none`**, **`is nav 'link' but holds N rows`**, **`is nav
  'link' but nests under '<p>'`**, **`nests under '<a>', a nav 'link' area`**, **`nests under
  '<a>', which is unpublished (nav 'none')`** — an area's `nav` key is closed. `link` is one
  page shown as one top-level sidebar link, so it holds one row and nothing nests in or under
  it; `none` leaves the area off the site, so every area nested under it is `none` too. Leave
  the key out for an area with a hub and a sidebar group.
- **`area '<a>' label "…" holds an em-dash`**, **`… page '<p>': label "…" holds an em-dash`** — a
  label names the area or the page, and a tagline after a dash belongs in the area's
  `hub.description`. Cut the label at the dash and move the tagline there.
- **`docs/data/site-structure.json: unreadable: …`** — the file does not parse, or has no
  `areas` list; no other check ran. Fix it, or restore it from git.

## Tags

Every page under `docs/` carries 2-5 tags from `docs/data/tags.json`, exactly one topic first,
then skills, then languages; [the tag reference](tags.md) lists them. Set a KB page's tags
with `node scripts/kb.mjs set <id> --tags '[…]'`; any other page is edited in place.

- **`<page>: no topic tag`**, **`<page>: N topic tags (a, b)`**, **`tags are out of facet order at
  "x"`** — pick the one topic the page is about and write it first, then the skills, then the
  languages. `docs/data/allow/tags.json` excuses these three on the pages a retag batch has not
  reached yet, and nothing else.
- **`<page>: unknown tag "x"`**, **`tag "x" does not apply to a page`**, **`N tags — a page
  carries 2-5`**, **`tag "x" is written twice`** — use a term the list holds, 2-5 of them.
- **`<page>: tags is not an inline list`** — write `tags: [a, b]`; a block list reads as no
  tags at all.
- **`site/src/lib/types.ts: TAGS is missing "x"`**, or **`TAGS lists "x", which is not a
  term`** — the tuple and the list hold the same ids; add or remove it in both, in one change.
  An id commented out of the tuple is not in it.
- **`TAGS lists "x" more than once`**, **`TAGS runs out of facet order at "x"`** — the tuple
  holds each id once, topics first, then skills, then languages, the order a page writes them.
- **``site/src/lib/types.ts: no `const TAGS = [...]` holding only quoted ids``** — the tuple is
  no longer one flat list of quoted ids with commas between them (comments are fine), so it
  was not checked at all. Write it back in that shape.
- **`docs/data/tags.json: no page under docs/ is tagged from it`** — the gate found no page to
  measure: the scan set is wrong, or the run is not at the repo root.
- **`docs/data/tags.json: term "x" is used by no page — a dead member`** — tag the page that
  earns the term, or retire the term from `docs/data/tags.json` and from the tuple.
- **`docs/data/tags.json: term …`** (missing key, unknown facet, a topic with no label, a label
  on a skill, a shared heading, a duplicate id) — the list itself is unsound, so no page was
  measured. Fix the term in `docs/data/tags.json`, then `make taxonomy`.
- **`docs/data/allow/tags.json: entry "x" excuses nothing`** — its retag batch has landed;
  delete the entry.

## Tag reference in sync

- **`FAIL: docs/reference/tags.md is STALE — run: make taxonomy`**, then diff lines — the page
  differs from what `tools/src/gen/gen-taxonomy.ts` renders from `docs/data/tags.json`. Run
  `make taxonomy` (`make gen` runs it too) and commit the page with the list; never edit it by
  hand.
- **`docs/data/tags.json: is not a tag list`** or **`is missing`** — the list the page is built
  from is gone or misshapen; the **Tags** gate names what is wrong with it.

## Site colour tokens

Reads the stylesheets under `site/src`, no build needed (`tools/src/gates/check-site-tokens.ts`).
A colour is decided once, in `site/src/styles/tokens.css`; every other stylesheet names it.

- **`site/src/<file>.css:<line>: \`#…\` is a colour literal`** (or `rgb(…)`, `hsl(…)`) — a
  typed colour, which reads right in one theme and wrong in the other. Use Starlight's
  `--sl-color-*` custom property, or a `--kb-*` token. A value nothing gives goes into
  `tokens.css` once, under a name, and the stylesheet uses the name.
- **a literal in a comment, `currentColor`, `transparent` or a named colour** is never a
  finding; nor is hex-like text that is no colour, such as an id selector.
- **`site/src does not exist`** — the gate runs from the repository root, where the site
  workspace lives.

## Site hook parity

Reads the site's markup and behaviour modules as text, no build needed
(`tools/src/gates/check-site-hooks.ts`). `data-kb-*` hooks are the only wiring between a
component's markup and its module, so the two must name the same ones.

- **`<module>.client.ts:<line>: data-kb-<x> is queried here and no site markup emits it`** — a
  hook was renamed or dropped in the markup (`.astro`, `.mdx`, or the diagram figure in
  `tools/src/lib/site-markdown.ts`) and the module still looks for the old name. Rename one side
  to match the other.
- **`<markup>:<line>: data-kb-<x> is emitted here and nothing reads it`** — no module queries
  it, no stylesheet keys on it, no program under `tools/src` looks for it: often the other half
  of a rename, where a second template still carries the old name. Rename it back or delete
  it. A hook that exists only for a person or an agent reading the built page gets an entry in
  `docs/data/allow/site-hooks.json` saying who reads it.
- **`docs/data/allow/site-hooks.json: entry "<name>" excuses nothing`** — the hook it excused
  is gone or now read: delete the entry.

## Hook suite (bash)

- **`tests/hooks/<hook>.test.sh:<line>: <assertion label>`** — that assertion failed. The file's
  header says what it proves; `bash tests/run.sh <hook> -v` replays the file with every
  assertion and the expected and actual values under the failure. A label opening with a
  scenario id (`hooks-O1:`) names the spec criterion the hook no longer meets.
- **`<file>: harness: …`** or **`failed without a parsed assertion`** — the file crashed, ran no
  assertion, or lost `tests/lib.sh`'s EXIT trap. Read its transcript with the command above.
- **`<data file> has an advisory case`** failing — a file under `docs/data/` has no case in
  `.claude/hooks/after-write.sh`. Add one naming what reads the file and the command to run.
- **`tests/run.sh: is missing`**, or **`exited 1 and named no failing test`** — the runner is
  gone or found no test file. Restore it from version control; `make install` if `jq` or `bash`
  is missing from the machine.

## Gate suite (vitest)

- **`<test file>: <test name> — <error>`** — that test fails. `make tools-test T=<file>` runs
  the file with vitest's full report.
- **`<test file>: failed to run — <error>`** — the file did not load: an import that does not
  resolve, or a throw at its top level.
- **`tools/vitest.config.ts: coverage for <metric> is N%, below its floor of M%`** — new code
  landed without the tests that cover it. Cover it; never lower a floor to land a change.
- **`tools/vitest.config.ts: is missing`** — the suite's config, which holds the floors, is gone.
  Restore it.
- **`vitest exited N and named no failing test or floor`** — vitest failed before it could
  report: usually not installed (`make install`), or a config error that `make tools-test`
  prints in full.

## Site portability

Runs after the site is built (`make site-build`, CI job `site`), over `site/dist/`. Every
finding is about a built page, so the repair is almost always in the build, not in the page.

- **`site/dist/<page>.html:<line>: root-absolute reference href="/…"`** — a link or source the
  post-build pass did not make relative. A stale `site/dist/` is the usual cause: run
  `make site-build`. If it stays red, the reference sits where the pass does not look (inside a
  script body, say) or a component writes a `/…` URL after the pass: write internal links
  root-absolute in the source and let `tools/src/site/site-portable.ts` rewrite them.
- **`positive tabindex`** — something set `tabindex` above 0, which reorders the keyboard walk.
  Use `0` or `-1`.
- **`a <script type="module"> carrying data-kb`** — a script of ours became a module, which
  never runs from `file://`. Ship behaviour in the classic bundle (`site/src/client/index.ts`).
- **`no <meta name="kb:level" …>`** or **`no skip link`** — the page lost its head facts or
  Starlight's skip link: a component override or a post-build pass dropped it.
- **`index.json` or `search-index.js is missing or empty`** — the post-build passes did not run
  or failed: run `make site-build` and read the first red step.
- **`is a built page search cannot find`**, **`indexes <route>, and no such page was built`**,
  **`offers <route>#<id> … no element with that id`** — the payload and the pages disagree. A
  stale build again, or a heading id that changed: rebuild, and if the id changed on purpose,
  nothing else needs doing.
- **`no built site at site/dist`** — build first: `make site-build`.

## Site noise and data layer

Runs after the site is built (`make site-build`, CI job `site`), over `site/dist/`
(`tools/src/gates/check-site-absence.ts`, the noise half in `tools/src/lib/site-noise.ts`).
Both halves state their rule in their headers.

The data layer: a fact is a bare `data-*` on an element with no `class`, carrying nothing but
`data-*` and an `id`; `data-kb-*` is a hook and never a fact.

- **`fact data-<x> on the classed element <tag class="…">`** — a fact landed on decoration. If
  a site plugin or component wrote it, wrap the classed element in a class-free `<div>` carrying
  the fact (`tools/src/lib/site-markdown.ts` does this for code frames and diagrams). If Starlight
  or another generator writes the attribute as its own state, add it to `VENDOR` in the gate
  with the reason.
- **`data block <tag> carries <attribute>`** — a class-free element with a fact also carries a
  foreign attribute (`title`, `role`, …). Move the attribute to an element inside, or the fact
  out to a wrapper.
- **`the knowledge region is not one <article> carrying exactly data-page, data-level,
  data-area, data-tags`** — the post-build pass did not wrap the page, or something else sits
  beside the article: run `make site-build`.
- **`a skip marker … inside the knowledge region`** — chrome was marked inside the article, so
  a machine reader would drop knowledge. Only chrome outside the knowledge region is skipped.
- **`no knowledge region`**, **`2 knowledge regions`** or **`no class-free data-page-head block
  holds the H1`** — the element carrying `data-kb-region`, which
  `site/src/components/MarkdownContent` writes around the rendered body, is missing or doubled,
  or a page lost the title block `PageTitle.astro` renders.

The noise:

- **`not at the formatter’s fixed point`** — a page changed after the build's last step, the
  formatter (`tools/src/site/site-format.ts`). Run `make site-build`. A **`formatting would
  change the page at character <n>`** finding is the formatter refusing a page it would change:
  the printer misread markup, so fix `site-format.ts`, never the page.
- **`<n> kb.js script tag(s)`** or **`the kb.js bundle loads as a module`** — every page loads
  its behaviour from exactly one classic `kb.js`, which `site/src/components/Head` emits; a
  module never runs from a folder.
- **`an inline <script type="module">`** — code in the page text. There is no allowlist for
  it: move the code into the bundle.
- **`unnamed external script`**, **`unnamed inline script`**, **`unnamed stylesheet`**,
  **`unnamed noscript style`**, **`<n> main stylesheet link(s)`**, **`no noscript style`** —
  something the allowlists in `tools/src/lib/site-noise.ts` do not name. The lists are this
  site's audit of what its build emits. A Starlight or Astro upgrade that renames a chunk or
  rewrites a snippet is the moment to re-audit: add an entry with its reason, or stop shipping
  it, never widen a pattern to fit. A changed `<noscript>` line in
  `site/src/components/Head/Head.astro` changes `NOSCRIPT_STYLE` with it.
- **`… on the not-found page`**, **`<n> style element(s) on the not-found page`** or **`the
  not-found page's style …`** — `404.html` is the one page held to its own rule: a host serves it
  at the address that missed, so it loads no stylesheet, script, icon or other file and carries
  exactly one small inline style that fetches nothing. The post-build pass writes it
  (`tools/src/site/site-not-found.ts`); a finding means something in `404.mdx` or that pass put a
  file link back. See [hosting the site](../concepts/hosting-the-site.md).
- **`the allowlist entry '<id>' … matched nothing`** — an entry names what the build no longer
  emits. Drop it.
- **`a <style> element outside a vector graphic and a noscript`**, **`a presentational
  style="…"`**, **`an on<event> attribute`** — paint or behaviour written into the page. Move
  it to the component's stylesheet or the bundle; only custom properties stay inline.
- **`unmarked chrome <nav|header|footer|aside …> outside the knowledge region`** — a landmark a
  machine reader cannot tell from knowledge. Ours carries `data-kb-skip` on its root; one the
  generator writes joins `STARLIGHT_CHROME` in `tools/src/site/site-portable.ts`.
- **`site/dist/<file>.js: a script file no page loads`** — the post-build pass prunes these by
  reachability; one that survived means the pass missed it. Run `make site-build`.

## Site accessibility floor

Runs after the site is built (`make site-build`, CI job `site`), over `site/dist/`
(`tools/src/gates/check-site-a11y.ts`). What markup answers without a browser.

- **`missing lang attribute on <html>`**, **`<n> <h1> elements`**, **`<n> heading(s) before
  the <h1>`** — the page frame or a component wrote the wrong outline: fix the component.
- **`aria reference '<id>' names no id on the page`** — an `aria-labelledby` or
  `aria-describedby` points at nothing. Fix the id on the component that writes both.
- **`role="option" … with no role="listbox" ancestor`** — an option outside its listbox.
- **`<img …> has no alt attribute`** — describe the image, or write `alt=""` for decoration.
- **`<svg …> has no accessible name`** — a graphic with no `<title>`, `aria-label` or resolving
  `aria-labelledby`. A diagram is named where it is framed (`rehypeKbDiagrams` in
  `tools/src/lib/site-markdown.ts`); an icon is `aria-hidden="true"`.
- **`a hub page whose only heading is its <h1>`** — `SectionHub.astro` renders group labels as
  headings; a hub without them has no outline.
- **`<tag class="kb-…"> is reached by no :focus-visible selector`** — a kb control with no
  focus ring. The floor is the shared rule in `site/src/styles/primitives.css`.
- **`<n>% of the page text is chrome (cap 80%)`** — most of the page's text is navigation.
  Restructure the page, or add a reasoned entry to `CHROME_ALLOWLIST` in the gate (it ships
  empty). A note saying an allowlisted page is back under the cap means its entry can go; a
  note that a page is in the warning band (`CHROME_BAND`) is a sign the page is filling up with
  chrome and is no failure by itself.
- **`<n> page(s) sit in the chrome warning band, above the <m> the ratchet allows`** — the band
  is a ratchet: `bandMax` in `docs/data/allow/site-a11y.json` is the most pages it may hold, and
  more pages than that fail. Trim the chrome of the pages the notes name above it. A note
  `only <n> page(s) sit in the warning band` means `bandMax` can drop to `<n>`; it only goes down.

## Site accessibility in a browser

Runs after the site is built (`make site-build`, CI job `site`): every page of `site/dist/`
opened from disk in headless Chromium, in both themes, checked by axe-core at WCAG 2.1 A and
AA (`tools/src/gates/check-site-axe.ts`). A second pass takes the home page and the first
pattern page through four states, each in both themes: the search dialog open with a query
typed, the phone menu drawer open at 390px, and the page at rest at 390px and at 800px.

- **`<rule> [<theme>, <impact>]: … at <selector> — … — <help link>`**, or from the second
  pass **`<rule> [<theme>, <state>, <impact>]: …`** — one violation in one theme and, for the
  second pass, in one state: `search open`, `menu open at 390px`, `at rest at 390px` or
  `at rest at 800px`. The dialog's rows and the drawer's links are the same markup on every
  page, so a state finding names the first page that shows it, not the only one. No state
  carries a waiver: `STATE_WAIVERS` ships empty. A contrast failure is a colour: fix the token in
  `site/src/styles/tokens.css`, never a literal in a component. Anything else is markup: fix
  the component or the post-build pass that writes it (`scrollable-region-focusable`, for one,
  is `focusScrollableCode` and `wrapScrollableTables` in `tools/src/site/site-portable.ts`).
- **`could not launch Chromium — run make site-deps`** — the browser is missing or broken.
- **`skipped: no Chromium installed`** on stdout — a clean exit with nothing checked; run
  `make site-deps` and the gate again.
- **`no Chromium installed and KB_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1`** — the environment demands a browser
  (CI's `site` job sets it, so a runner without one cannot pass by checking nothing): run
  `make site-deps`.

## Site size budget

Runs after the site is built (`make site-build`, CI job `site`), over `site/dist/`
(`tools/src/gates/check-site-budget.ts`). Every number is in its `BUDGETS` constant beside the
value it was set from; gzip sizes are level 9, what a host's compression reaches.

- **`<page>.html: is N bytes, over the page budget of M; biggest part: …`** (or `…gzipped…`, or
  the tighter budget for a page that is not a case study, or for a hub) — a page grew. The
  message names the part that holds most of it: inline diagrams and their style blocks, inline
  scripts, navigation or tables. Trim that part at its source under `docs/`, or in the
  component or markdown plugin that writes it.
- **`<file>: is N bytes, over its budget of M; biggest part: …`** — the bundle
  (`kb.<hash>.js`), the search payload (`search-index.<hash>.js`) or the manifest
  (`index.json`) grew. For the payload and the manifest the message names the field that holds
  most of it; the payload's fields are written by `tools/src/site/gen-search-index.ts`.
- **`loads N bytes of blocking stylesheets, over the budget of M`** — a page's stylesheets
  (the main one, the code frames' and any shared diagram style) sum past the budget; the message
  names the biggest.
- **`needs N bytes gzipped before its first render, over the budget of M`** — the page's HTML,
  its blocking stylesheets and its synchronous scripts; the message names the biggest.
- **`asks for N files … over the budget of M`** — a script, a stylesheet or an icon too many.
- **`<file>: is missing — the build writes it`** — the bundle, payload or manifest is absent:
  `make site-build`.
- **A budget that must move.** Measure the built site again, write the new value and what it was
  measured from beside it in `BUDGETS`, and say why in the change. A host that does not compress
  is no reason: [hosting the site](../concepts/hosting-the-site.md) says what it must do.

## Site reader flows

Runs on its own after the site is built (`make site-e2e` after `make site-build`, CI job
`site`), never inside the build: fifty-five flows under `tools/e2e/`, each run four ways — the
built site from disk and from a local static server, at a 1600px desktop and a 390px phone —
