and the fourteen flows tagged `@tablet` once more, from the server at 800px, the width where
cards sit side by side while the sidebar is still a drawer
(`tools/src/gates/check-site-e2e.ts` wraps Playwright). The routes a flow visits are picked in
`tools/e2e/fixtures.ts` from `docs/data/site-structure.json` and `site/dist/index.json`.

- **`FAIL <flow>: [<project>] <what> (tools/e2e/<spec>.spec.ts:<line>)`** — that flow broke in
  that project. Rerun it alone with its browser window:
  `node node_modules/@playwright/test/cli.js test -c tools/e2e/playwright.config.ts -g <flow> --headed`.
  Red in every project is usually the component the flow drives (`site/src/components/`); red
  only on `file-*` is something that needs a server, such as a module script; red only on
  `*-phone` is the drawer or the layout below 72rem, and red only on `served-tablet` is a
  layout between the two (the cards below 50rem, the drawer below 76rem).
- **`FAIL deep-link: …`** — a link with a `#fragment` landed wrong: the target is under the
  sticky header, a `<details>` around it stayed closed, or `:target` painted nothing
  (`site/src/styles/primitives.css`). The ids are read from the built pages, so a page that
  lost the id fails in `tools/e2e/fixtures.ts` instead, naming the kind of page it wanted.
- **`console errors in the flow "<flow>" that EXPECTED_CONSOLE … does not name`** — a page
  script threw or logged an error while the flow ran. A message that is a known debt is named,
  with its reason and flows, in `EXPECTED_CONSOLE` in `tools/e2e/fixtures.ts`; an entry whose
  flow stops printing it fails too, so delete it when the cause is fixed.
- **A flow that passes once and fails once** — a flake. Run `make site-e2e-repeat`, which runs
  every flow three times in a row; a flow that fails there is waiting on something it does not
  wait for. Fix the wait (an `expect` that polls), never add a retry.
- **`the link "<href>" leads to <route>, which is no built page`** — a link a flow followed
  (sidebar, card, pager, search row) points at nothing. The component writing that href is at
  fault, or the page moved without its row in `docs/data/site-structure.json`.
- **`the run itself failed: no built page is …`** — a fixture found no page of the kind a flow
  needs (a diagram beside a sketch, a prerequisite card). Rebuild; if it stays, the site lost
  that kind of page, and the flow or its pick in `tools/e2e/fixtures.ts` has to change with it.
- **`playwright exited <n> and named no failing flow`** — the runner broke before any flow,
  most often the served projects' port (4719) already in use: stop what holds it, or set
  `KB_E2E_PORT`.
- **`skipped: no Chromium installed`** on stdout — a clean exit with nothing run; run
  `make site-deps` and the gate again. With `KB_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1` set (CI's `site` job does),
  the same absence is **`no Chromium installed and KB_REQUIRE_BROWSER=1`**, a finding.
- **`flow "x" skipped in <n> project(s)`**, **`more than the <m> its entry allows`**, **`entry
  "x" allows <m> skip(s) … but <n> happened`** — the skipped flows are pinned in
  `docs/data/allow/site-e2e.json`, one entry per flow with its `count` and reason. A flow that
  skips more often, or that has no entry, is a regression in what it needs (a draft page, a
  phone width): fix that. An entry allowing more than happened is stale: lower or delete it.
- **`no built site at site/dist`** — build first: `make site-build`.

## Site built links

Runs after the site is built (`make site-build`, CI job `site`), over `site/dist/`
(`tools/src/gates/check-site-links.ts`). A link resolves when a file is on disk there, since
the site opens from a folder.

- **`site/dist/<page>.html: link '<url>' → <path> does not exist`** — a link to a page or file
  that was not built. Rebuild first (`make site-build`); if it stays, the source page links
  what is not there: fix the page under `docs/` and rebuild.
- **`… is a folder, not a page`** — a link naming a folder, which opens nothing from disk.
  Link the folder's hub page (`<folder>.html`) instead.
- **`… has no element with id '<id>'`** — the fragment matches no `id` or `name` on the target,
  or only one inside a code sample, which is text. A heading was reworded or an id changed.
- **`link '<url>' climbs out of the site root`** — one `../` too many.
- **`link '<url>' is root-absolute`** — a link starting with one `/`, which opens nothing from a
  folder. The post-build pass makes every link relative, so a stale or partial build is the
  usual cause: run `make site-build`.
- **`link 'https://github.com/…/blob/main/<path>' → <path> is no file in this repository`** —
  a page under `docs/` links a file the site does not publish, so the build sent the link to
  GitHub, and no such file is in the tree: usually a typo in the link. `make validate`'s
  repository-links gate names the same line. Fix the link in the page and rebuild.
- **`is a folder of pages with no hub page`** — a folder of built pages whose hub
  (`<folder>.html` beside it, or `index.html` at the root) was not built: the structure file
  has no area for it.
- **`is linked from no hub`** or **`is linked from 2 hubs`** — every page but the home page
  belongs to exactly one hub's list. Only links in a hub's knowledge region count, up to its
  next-steps section; the sidebar and the breadcrumbs do not. Put the page in one area of
  `docs/data/site-structure.json`.
- **`lists <page> before <page> in one group, against the reading order`** — within one group
  of a hub (the entries under one `<h2>`), the area's pages must follow the structure file's
  order; the hub generator (`orderHub` in `tools/src/site/gen-site-hubs.ts`) keeps it. A stale
  build, or a change to the generator or to `SectionHub` that reorders entries: rebuild with
  `make site-build`, and if it stays red, fix the reordering, not the order in the file.
- **`docs/data/learning-paths.json: profile "<id>" stage <route> matches no built page`** — a
  learning path walks a page that is not built: the page was renamed or removed. Fix the stage
  in the file and run `make gen`.
- **`docs/data/site-structure.json: is not readable JSON`** or
  **`docs/data/learning-paths.json: is not readable`** — the gate reads which pages are hubs,
  and the stages to check, from these files: `make gate G=check-json` names the parse error.
- **`no built site at site/dist`** or **`no .html files under site/dist`** — build first:
  `make site-build`.

## Build the site

The CI step `Build the site` runs `make site-compile`: lint over `site/`, the site's unit tests,
then `npm run build` in `site/` (the mirror and hubs, the bundle, `astro check`, Astro, the
post-build passes). Its own output names the step that failed.

- **`[gen-site-docs] FAIL docs/<path>.md: is missing required frontmatter: …`** — a published
  page lacks a key the site needs. Add it to the page's frontmatter.
- **`astro check` or the build names a page and a key** (`area`, `level`, `tags`) — a value
  outside its closed list: the areas are `docs/data/site-structure.json`, the tags
  `docs/data/tags.json`.
- **a stale page after a plugin change** — Astro caches rendered markdown: `make site-rebuild`.

## Install repo tooling

- **`npm ci` fails on the lockfile** — `package-lock.json` disagrees with a `package.json`. Run
  `npm install` locally and commit the lockfile with the manifest change.
- **every gate step is skipped** — a setup step failed, and gate steps run only after setup
  succeeded. The first red step in the job is the one to read.

## Deployed site answers

Runs after every deploy, as the `smoke` job of `.github/workflows/pages.yml`
(`tools/src/site/site-smoke.ts`), and nowhere else: not in `make validate`, not on a pull request.
It asks the live site a handful of questions (the index, the two published schemas, `llms.txt`,
one page's record and a path the site lacks) and never crawls. The deploy is done before it
starts, so a red `smoke` job means the site is live and something it serves is wrong; nothing is
rolled back. It waits up to eleven minutes for the live `index.json` to be the one the build
wrote: GitHub Pages lets a CDN keep a file for ten minutes and ignores the query string in its
cache key, so a copy cached just before a deploy can outlive the deploy by that long, and a
shorter wait would blame the build for it. In a finding `<root>` is
the address the deploy reported, such as `https://odere-pro.github.io/patterns-kb/`. Reproduce a
run from a checkout of the deployed commit with
`node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/src/site/site-smoke.ts --url <published root> --index-sha <sha256 of site/dist/index.json>`;
without `--index-sha` it asks once and waits for nothing.

- **`<root>index.json still serves sha256 <a>, not the sha256 <b> the build wrote`** — after the
  whole wait the host serves another build, so the run stops there: nothing else the host serves
  can be trusted to be this build's. Re-run the `smoke` job from the run's page, since a CDN can
  take longer than the wait to take a deploy and a re-run starts a new wait. If it stays red, a
  later deploy replaced this one (its own `smoke` job is the one to read) or this one never
  reached the host (read the run's `deploy` job).
- **`<root>index.json answered HTTP 404, not 200`**, and the same for `llms.txt`, a schema or the
  record — the host holds no such file. Re-run first, since the host may still be on a build that
  had none. If it stays red, run `make site-build` and look in `site/dist/`: a file missing there
  is the build's fault, and the `site-portable` gate names it.
- **`<root>index.json could not be fetched: fetch failed (<cause>)`** or **`answered HTTP 503, not
  200`** — the host did not answer: a reset connection, a request past its ten seconds or a
  server error. The index is asked again for the whole wait and every other address once, so
  re-run the job; if it repeats, the host is down, which is not the repo's fault.
- **`<root>index.json is served as "<type>", not application/json`** or **`is not valid JSON`** —
  the host sent something other than the file. GitHub Pages serves `.json` as `application/json`,
  so another type means a page or a proxy answered in the file's place: look at what sits in
  front of Pages (a custom domain, a redirect rule) before the build.
- **`<root>index.json breaks kb-index-1: <pointer>: <message> (<keyword>)`**, at most five of
  them, then **`in N more place(s)`** — the index on the host does not hold the published schema.
  Re-run once to rule out an old build. If it repeats, run `make site-build` and the
  `site-portable` gate; the pointer says where in the file the fault is.
- **`<root><record route> breaks kb-record-1: …`** or **`has id "x", but <root>index.json lists
  the page as "y"`** — the first pattern's record on the host does not hold the schema, or is not
  the page the index says. An invalid record is the build's fault: run `make site-build`, then
  the `site-portable` and `kb-record-schema` gates, which hold every record. A valid record with
  another id means the index and the record came from different builds (re-run), or the index
  names the wrong file as the record.
- **`tools/src/contract/schema/<file>.json: differs from the deployed copy at
  <root>schema/<file>.json`** — the finding gives both sizes and sha256 digests. The deploy
  served an old build (re-run to rule it out), or the file in the repo was edited and not
  deployed, or the build did not copy it: run `make site-build` and compare
  `site/dist/schema/<file>.json` with the repo's file.
- **`<root>llms.txt is served as "<type>", not as plain text`** or **`is empty`** — a page
  answered in the file's place, or the build wrote it empty. Same repair as a missing file: run
  `make site-build` and read `site/dist/llms.txt`.
- **`<root>__kb_missing__.json answered HTTP 200, not 404`** — the host answers a path the site
  lacks with a page. GitHub Pages answers a miss with `404.html` and status 404, so a 200 comes
  from outside the build: the Pages settings (a custom domain or proxy that sends misses to the
  home page) or a change to `404.html` or the step that builds it. Check that `make site-build`
  still writes `site/dist/404.html`, and see
  [hosting the site](../concepts/hosting-the-site.md).
- **`--url is required`**, **`--index-sha "" is not a sha256: 64 lower-case hex digits`**
  (exit 2) — the workflow passed an empty value. Read the `build` job's step "Fingerprint the
  built index" and the `deploy` job's `page_url`.
- **`tools/src/contract/schema/<file>.json: is missing`** — the checkout holds no copy of a
  published schema to compare with, so nothing was asked. Restore the file; the contract names
  the schemas in `tools/src/contract/contract.ts`.
